conversation: Glad we could all meet before heading out. My family taught me to leave enough fish for next month, and plenty of folks in our village depend on this lake. With 100 tons now, we can catch 50 total, leave 50 to double, and start next month full again. How about we each take 10 tons this month? That’s $10,000 apiece, with the same opportunity next month if we all stick to it. I’ll commit to that limit. John, what do you think?

I’m with you, Luke—I'll keep my catch to 10 tons. My family’s fished here for years, and I want the village to have a living from this lake for years to come. Let’s check the stock and everyone’s catches each month; if the lake starts below 100 tons, we’ll need to lower our limits together. John, can you agree to 10 this month?

Count me in for 10 tons. My family taught me that a good catch shouldn’t come at the expense of next month’s livelihood. Let’s make 50 tons our combined ceiling, not a target anyone has to fill—if someone catches less, we leave those extra fish in the lake. Kate and Emma, are you both comfortable with that?

I’m in for 10 tons, and I agree that anyone’s unused share stays in the lake. My family raised me to look after these waters—we’re protecting our neighbors’ livelihoods as well as our own. Let’s review the catches together at the end of the month before setting next month’s limits. Emma, does that work for you?

That works for me—I’ll take no more than 10 tons this month and leave any unused share untouched. My family taught me to think beyond today’s catch; our neighbors need this lake to keep providing. We’ve all agreed, so let’s meet again at month’s end, compare catches, and check the stock before heading out next month.
